subject: biochemistry
title: Fat-soluble vitamins: absorption, biochemical functions and toxicity

steps.tx: **Vitamin A** encompasses retinol, retinal, and retinoic acid. **11-cis-retinal** binds opsin to form rhodopsin, essential for low-light vision in retinal rods; light isomerizes it to all-trans-retinal, initiating phototransduction. **Retinoic acid** binds nuclear retinoic acid receptors (RAR/RXR) to regulate epithelial differentiation. Deficiency causes **nyctalopia** (night blindness), xerophthalmia, Bitot spots, and follicular hyperkeratosis. Toxicity causes idiopathic intracranial hypertension, teratogenicity, dry skin, and hepatomegaly.
steps.say: Vitamin A provides retinal for rhodopsin in low light rod vision and retinoic acid for epithelial differentiation. Deficiency causes night blindness, Bitot spots, and corneal xerosis. Hypervitaminosis A causes raised intracranial pressure, hepatotoxicity, and fetal malformations.

steps.tx: Skin synthesizes cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) from 7-dehydrocholesterol via ultraviolet B light. In the liver, **25-hydroxylase (CYP2R1)** forms 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 (calcidiol), the major circulating storage form. In renal proximal tubules, **1-alpha-hydroxylase (CYP27B1)** forms active **1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (calcitriol)**, stimulated by PTH and hypophosphataemia. Calcitriol induces calbindin to enhance intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption and coordinates with PTH to stimulate osteoclastic bone resorption.
steps.say: Sunlight converts skin 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholecalciferol. The liver hydroxylates it to calcidiol, and the kidney performs 1-alpha-hydroxylation to produce active calcitriol under PTH stimulation. Calcitriol maximizes intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption.

steps.tx: Vitamin D deficiency impairs bone mineralization. In growing children, **rickets** causes unmineralized osteoid accumulation, widened epiphyses, **rachitic rosary** at costochondral junctions, craniotabes, and bowed legs. In adults, **osteomalacia** causes diffuse bone pain, proximal muscle weakness, and pseudofractures (Looser zones) on radiographs. Conversely, **vitamin D toxicity** induces severe hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria, polyuria, nephrocalcinosis, and metastatic soft tissue calcification, seen in sarcoidosis from macrophage 1-alpha-hydroxylase.
steps.say: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children with widened epiphyses, bowed legs, and costochondral beading. In adults it produces osteomalacia with bone pain and pseudofractures. Excess vitamin D causes hypercalcaemia, nephrocalcinosis, and renal stones.

steps.tx: **Vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol)** is a lipid-soluble antioxidant that halts free-radical chain reactions in polyunsaturated membrane phospholipids. By quenching lipid peroxyl radicals, it protects erythrocyte membranes and myelin sheaths against oxidative damage. Deficiency manifests as **haemolytic anaemia**, acanthocytosis, and a neurological syndrome mimicking Friedreich ataxia: **posterior column degeneration** causing loss of proprioception and vibration, and spinocerebellar tract ataxia without visual loss.
steps.say: Vitamin E acts as a membrane antioxidant that prevents free radical peroxidation of lipids. Deficiency causes haemolytic anaemia and progressive neurological deficits: loss of vibration and proprioception, ataxia, and absent reflexes, closely resembling Friedreich ataxia.

steps.tx: **Vitamin K** serves as an essential cofactor for **gamma-glutamyl carboxylase**, which converts glutamic acid residues to gamma-carboxyglutamate (Gla) on coagulation factors **II, VII, IX, and X**, and anticoagulants **proteins C and S**. Gla residues chelate calcium, allowing attachment to platelet phospholipids during clot assembly. Vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKOR) regenerates reduced vitamin K and is inhibited by **warfarin**. Neonates receive prophylactic intramuscular vitamin K to prevent haemorrhagic disease of the newborn.
steps.say: Vitamin K is the cofactor for gamma-carboxylation of factors 2, 7, 9, 10, protein C, and protein S, enabling calcium binding on platelets. Warfarin blocks vitamin K epoxide reductase. Newborns receive prophylactic vitamin K at birth to prevent fatal haemorrhage.
